title: test-instance
subtitle: Drop any PDF or notes → McCreary cook → learning instance
tagline: Upload a textbook PDF, lecture notes, syllabus, or prep guide - the McCreary stack cooks a learning graph, live MicroSim labs, and Bloom quizzes you can study inside Desk OS.
attribution: Demo of Dan McCreary’s open stack (github.com/dmccreary/microsims, claude-skills, intelligent-textbooks). CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Document examples are illustrative. Not affiliated with ACT, Inc. Original practice items only - no copyrighted exam stems reproduced.
mission: The product his GitHub is built for: take any study document (static PDF + notes + syllabus) and cook an intelligent learning instance - graph-backed chapters, interactive labs for weak spots, and quizzes that target Bloom levels - instead of another linear page-turner. This showcase later replaces ACT Field Book as the default cooked book.

chapters.title: From any document to a graph
chapters.body: Drop a prep guide, textbook chapter, lecture PDF, or syllabus. McCreary’s stack extracts the concept spine so every later artifact (chapter, sim, quiz, FAQ) hangs off the same DAG. This demo seed uses the Official ACT Prep Guide because it’s the richest public structure - the cook is document-agnostic.
outcomes: Name what kinds of documents the cook accepts
Explain why a learning graph beats a flat TOC for remediation
Point to where MicroSims attach (geometry, data, modeling)

chapters.title: English - conventions you can feel
chapters.body: When the source has writing/language sections, the cook keeps Production of Writing, Knowledge of Language, and Conventions nodes, adds a tight glossary, and pairs punctuation FAQs with short Bloom items - so rules stop being paragraphs you skim.
outcomes: Map a language miss to one graph node
Fix a modifier/punctuation issue with a rule + example

chapters.title: Math - draw it, then simulate it
chapters.body: Geometry and modeling chapters are where the MicroSim library punches hardest. Plane geometry, right triangles, slope - the source says ‘use illustrations.’ MicroSims are the illustration that moves: Pythagorean proof, triangle types, circle, slope-and-intercept, projectile for modeling stories.
outcomes: Solve a right-triangle item after using the Pythagorean MicroSim
Read slope from a live y=mx+b lab
Translate a wordy modeling stem into a simmable setup

chapters.title: Science - graphs you can push
chapters.body: When the document trains graph reading or experimental tradeoffs, the stack attaches labs that make axes and trends tactile (temp-and-pressure, projectile, Galton board) so ‘read the figure’ becomes a skill you rehearse.
outcomes: Extract the claim a graph actually supports
Compare two viewpoints without inventing data

chapters.title: The factory that cooks any book
chapters.body: claude-skills order: learning graph → glossary → chapters → MicroSims → quizzes → FAQs → concept validator → quality metrics. Point that pipeline at any study PDF and you get a Desk learning instance. Before (document) and After (intelligent book).
outcomes: List the 9 pipeline steps in order
Say which skill emits the learning graph
Name one MicroSim for a weak spot in your document

faqs.question: What documents can I drop in?
faqs.answer: Any study document the cook can parse: prep-guide PDFs, textbook chapters, lecture notes, syllabi. This showcase demos four types; the live seed is cooked from an Official ACT Prep Guide structure as the richest example.

faqs.question: What does McCreary’s GitHub actually do to a PDF?
faqs.answer: It doesn’t host copyrighted exam items. It turns the document’s structure (TOC, standards, headings) into a learning graph, then generates chapters, glossary, FAQs, MicroSim matches, and original Bloom quizzes - an intelligent textbook shell you study inside Desk OS.

faqs.question: Why MicroSims?
faqs.answer: Static figures don’t rehearse the move. MicroSims are illustrations you can change - angle, gravity, sample size - which builds the transfer practice items test.

faqs.question: Is this a replacement for the source book?
faqs.answer: No. Keep authentic practice tests and primary readings. This instance is the cooked layer: remediation paths, live labs, and targeted quizzes. Long-term it replaces ACT Field Book as MindCraft’s default cooked-book surface.

faqs.question: Which skill runs first?
faqs.answer: learning-graph-generator. Everything else (glossary, chapters, sims, quizzes, FAQs, validator, quality) assumes that DAG exists.

faqs.question: How is this different from act-fieldbook?
faqs.answer: act-fieldbook is MindCraft’s native ACT practice UI. test-instance is the McCreary-stack showcase: drop any document → cook → learn with live open MicroSims + the skills pipeline story.

faqs.question: Can it generate new quiz questions?
faqs.answer: Yes - quiz-generator writes original Bloom-aligned items per concept. This demo ships 16 originals (not copied from any copyrighted exam).

faqs.question: Where do the 116 sims come from?
faqs.answer: dmccreary/microsims on GitHub Pages. This showcase curates a relevant slice and deep-links into the real main.html / index.html labs.

questions.prompt: You drop a study PDF into the McCreary cook. What is the first durable artifact the skills should emit?
choices: A learning graph of concepts + prereqs
questions.explain: The learning graph is the spine - chapters, sims, quizzes, and FAQs all hang off it.

questions.prompt: A right triangle has legs 6 and 8. What is the hypotenuse?
questions.explain: 6-8-10 triangle (Pythagorean). The Pythagorean MicroSim makes this visual.

questions.prompt: In y = mx + b, what does m control on the graph?
questions.explain: m is slope. Slope & Intercept MicroSim lets you drag m and watch the line.

questions.prompt: When a cooked science section includes Data Representation, the safest first move is usually to:
questions.explain: Graph literacy starts with axes and units - then the questions.

questions.prompt: Which choice correctly shows possession for a singular noun?
A stem describes a ball thrown with angle and speed. Which MicroSim best rehearses the model?
questions.explain: Projectile Motion is the live model for that modeling story.

questions.prompt: Conflicting Viewpoints items mostly test whether you can:
choices: Compare what each scientist claims vs. what data shows
questions.explain: Evaluate competing claims - not content trivia.

choices: How the author builds meaning (word choice, structure, purpose)
questions.explain: Focus on author’s craft, not outside facts.

questions.prompt: A Galton board demo is most useful for which idea?
questions.explain: Statistics & Probability - distributions emerging from chance.

questions.prompt: In the Five Levels model, MicroSims primarily unlock:
questions.explain: Level 3 = interactive simulations inside the textbook.

questions.prompt: Good pacing for timed practice is closest to:
choices: Spend equal time on every item no matter what
Bank easy wins first, return to hard ones

questions.prompt: Before drafting a timed essay from a prompt, you should:
choices: Prewrite / plan using the prompt’s perspectives

questions.prompt: Why generate original Bloom quizzes instead of copying exam-book items?
choices: Copyright + unlimited targeted remediation on the graph
questions.explain: Keep authentic tests in the source; use generated items for graph-targeted reps.

questions.prompt: Temp & Pressure MicroSim best trains which move?
choices: Reading a relationship between two variables on a graph

questions.prompt: In a right triangle, sin(θ) is opposite/hypotenuse. Which lab builds that intuition?
questions.explain: Trig MicroSims make the ratio visible.

questions.prompt: A Level-5 tutor agent on a cooked graph should primarily:
choices: Walk the graph, launch the right MicroSim, assign the next Bloom item
questions.explain: Agent = navigate graph + tools (sims/quizzes), not skip real study.
